title: Listing URL Filtering rules and URL categories without truncation

checks.do: Whether a rule list that stops at a round number, such as 100, is truncated; re-read with a smaller page size when it is.
Whether the rule count matches the console when the list came from a raw SDK or API call, before reasoning about precedence.
Whether the category inventory is complete, by requesting every category type and checking the count against the console.

go-readallpages-1000.statement: The Go SDK's `GetAll` for URL Filtering rules walks pages through `common.ReadAllPages`, which requests `pageSize=1000` by default and stops at the first page shorter than the page size.

quotes: const defaultPageSize = 1000 // Default page size for most ZIA APIs

observed-100-of-133.statement: On a real tenant, an SDK-based read of URL Filtering rules returned 100 rules while the console showed 133; reading with `pageSize=100` and advancing until a short page returned all of them.
observed-100-of-133.conditions: Observed by the zscalerctl-dev maintainers on a production tenant (vendored zscaler-sdk-go v3.8.55); the validation record and its repeatable check are public.

quotes: The original downstream symptom was a 100-rule CLI result while the admin console showed 133 rules.
The reader requests `page=1&pageSize=100` and advances until a page contains fewer than 100 records.

silent-truncation.statement: Treat any rule list of exactly 100 (or any multiple) as possibly truncated: if the endpoint returns at most 100 rules per page, a 1000-record paginator reads the first page as "short" and stops without error.
silent-truncation.conditions: Inferred from the SDK's stop condition and the observed 100-of-133 result; the per-page server limit itself is not documented.

quotes: The original downstream symptom was a 100-rule CLI result while the admin console showed 133 rules.

python-single-request.statement: The Python SDK's `list_rules` sends one request with caller-chosen `page` and `page_size` and returns that page only; callers must page themselves.

categories-clamp-20.statement: Listing URL categories has been seen to clamp at 20 records; a complete inventory must request every category type and confirm the count against the console.
categories-clamp-20.conditions: Recorded by zscalerctl-dev as a live regression check for tenants with more than 20 URL and TLD categories.

quotes: `count` is greater than 20 and matches the corresponding console inventory;

page-size-limit.title: The maximum page size the URL Filtering rules endpoint honors
page-size-limit.blocks: stating the truncation mechanism as documented behavior
page-size-limit.detail: Behavior shows reads of 100 per page work and a 1000-size request returned 100. No source states the server-side limit.

getall-completeness.summary: Reading the Go SDK suggests GetAll returns every URL Filtering rule (it loops over pages until a short page); live reads show it can stop after the first page.

positions.says: GetAll walks pages, so its result reads as the complete rule list.

quotes: The original downstream symptom was a 100-rule CLI result while the admin console showed 133 rules.

positions.says: On a real tenant the read returned 100 of 133 rules.

getall-completeness.impact: An agent trusting the SDK reading reasons over an incomplete rule list, and the missing rule is often the one that wins.

resolution.note: SDK code establishes what the client does; only observation establishes what the API returns.
